sections.name: File setup (part 1)
sections.title: Lists the Python packages needed
sections.what: Lists the add-on libraries the app uses, grouped by purpose: data and maths, database, Excel export, web scraping, charts, notebooks, OpenAI, a web API framework, and small utilities. Each line asks for a minimum version.
sections.why: The comments label each group by its use. Reason not stated in the code for choosing minimum rather than exact versions.
sections.watch_out: Because there are no upper limits, a future major library release could break the app on a fresh install.

sections.name: File setup (part 2)
sections.title: Optional developer tools, currently disabled
sections.what: Lines that are all comments, listing optional tools for testing and checking code (pytest, black, flake8, mypy). Because they start with a hash mark, pip ignores them and installs none of these.
sections.why: Likely reason: kept as an option for developers without forcing them on everyday users.
sections.watch_out: Removing the hash mark from one of these lines is what turns it on; nothing in this packet runs these tools.

summary: List of Python add-on libraries the project needs, each with a minimum version.
purpose: Tells pip which packages to install so the app can run.
why: Likely reason: keeps the list of needed libraries in one readable file that the install script can use.
how: pip reads each line that is not a comment and installs the named package at the stated minimum version or newer. Lines starting with a hash mark are notes and are skipped.
inputs: No direct input. Read by pip when install.sh runs or when a user runs pip install with this file.
outputs: Installed packages inside the virtual environment.
risks: Only minimum versions are set, so a future major release of a library could break the app. The PDF export option needs system tools. The development tools are commented out and not installed.
debug: If installation fails, find the package named in the error and check its version. Run pip install -r requirements.txt without the quiet option to see full details. Confirm the Python version is 3.9 or newer.
